"This is a story of how harmless choices can make a harmful world."

The choice in question is: “I wanna move if less than 1/3 of my neighbors are like me.”

The result is that the squares and triangles, initially mixed, move into separate communities. This is supposed to serve as propaganda justifying racial quotas and other such forced racial discrimination to promote diversity:

"The takeaway ... is that demanding a single bit of diversity in your spaces makes a huge difference overall. For a real-world application of this idea, see Plz Diversify Your Panel, an initiative where overrepresented speakers refuse invitations to speak on panels that don't include diverse representation."

The right question to ask is: What is "harmful" about people freely choosing to form communities with similar people? Answer: nothing! To the contrary, this kind of voluntary association builds healthier and more cohesive communities. The Cultural Marxists' dogmatic belief that "diversity" and "multiculturalism" are desirable in any context, even if they have to be achieved by compulsion, is just that: dogma; without any rational justification whatever.

The closest thing to a reason that most of its supporters seem to have is: compulsory racial segregation was an evil, therefore compulsory integration (taken to be its opposite) is a good.

But the reality is that what was evil about segregation was precisely the fact that it was imposed on people by coercion and compulsion. Compulsory integration is exactly as bad as compulsory segregation. (Yes, I know that the "game" creators did not EXPLICITLY call for compulsion.
